steps.title: Import Vue and the Composition API functions (ref, onMounted, onUnmounted)
steps.instruction: Import ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted from 'vue'
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Composition API functions from the Vue package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing multiple functions
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.seedCode: // Import ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue Composition API functions ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted are imported from 'vue'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Vue Composition API functions needed for reactive state and lifecycle hooks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing all three functions: ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the useWindowSize composable function
steps.instruction: Define a function named useWindowSize that returns an empty object for now.
steps.hint: Create a function declaration or arrow function with the name useWindowSize and have it return an empty object {}.
steps.seedCode:
// Import ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted from 'vue'

// Define the useWindowSize function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A useWindowSize function is defined and returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The code includes a function named useWindowSize that returns an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the useWindowSize composable function. This will be the foundation for tracking window dimensions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a function named useWindowSize that returns an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on creating the function. Define a function named useWindowSize that returns an empty object {}.

steps.title: Initialize reactive width and height state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the useWindowSize function, create two reactive variables using ref: one named width and one named height, both initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Use the ref function imported from 'vue' to create reactive references. For example: const count = ref(0).
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWindowSize function will contain two reactive state variables: width and height, both initialized to 0.
successCriteria: The useWindowSize function contains width and height variables created with ref(), both initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created reactive state for the window dimensions using ref.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created both width and height refs, both initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside useWindowSize, create two variables using ref(): width and height, both set to 0.

steps.title: Define the updateWindowSize handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the useWindowSize function, define a function named updateWindowSize that updates the width and height refs with the current window dimensions.
steps.hint: Create a function that sets width.value to window.innerWidth and height.value to window.innerHeight.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWindowSize function now contains an updateWindowSize handler that can update the reactive width and height values.
successCriteria: The updateWindowSize function is defined inside useWindowSize and sets width.value and height.value to window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight respectively.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the updateWindowSize handler that will update the reactive dimensions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it sets both width.value and height.value to the current window dimensions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateWindowSize function isn't defined correctly. It should update both width and height refs with window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.

steps.title: Set up the resize event listener with onMounted
steps.instruction: Inside the useWindowSize function, call onMounted to add a 'resize' event listener to the window that calls the updateWindowSize function.
steps.hint: Use onMounted(() => { window.addEventListener('resize', updateWindowSize); }) to set up the event listener when the component mounts.
steps.expectedOutcome: The onMounted lifecycle hook is used to attach a resize event listener to the window, which will call updateWindowSize whenever the window size changes.
successCriteria: onMounted is called with a callback that adds a 'resize' event listener to the window, and the listener calls updateWindowSize.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the resize event listener using onMounted. This ensures the window size is tracked when the component mounts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling onMounted with a callback that adds the event listener to the window and calls updateWindowSize.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to use onMounted to add a 'resize' event listener to the window that calls updateWindowSize.

steps.title: Clean up the event listener with onUnmounted
steps.instruction: Inside the useWindowSize function, call onUnmounted to remove the 'resize' event listener from the window.
steps.hint: Use onUnmounted with a callback function that calls window.removeEventListener('resize', updateWindowSize).
steps.expectedOutcome: The resize event listener will be properly cleaned up when the component using useWindowSize is unmounted, preventing memory leaks.
successCriteria: onUnmounted is called with a callback that removes the 'resize' event listener using window.removeEventListener.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've properly set up cleanup for the resize event listener using onUnmounted.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling onUnmounted with a callback that removes the event listener.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to call onUnmounted to clean up the event listener when the component is unmounted.

steps.title: Return the reactive width and height from the composable
steps.instruction: At the end of the useWindowSize function, return an object containing the width and height refs.
steps.hint: In Vue composables, you typically return reactive values so they can be used in components. Use return { width, height }.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWindowSize function now returns an object with width and height refs, making these reactive values available to any component that uses this composable.
successCriteria: The useWindowSize function returns an object containing both width and height refs.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the reactive width and height from the composable. This allows components to destructure and use these values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning an object that contains both width and height refs from the useWindowSize function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useWindowSize function needs to return an object with width and height refs. Try adding `return { width, height }` at the end of the function.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Define a Vue component named App with a setup function that returns an empty template.
steps.hint: Use the Vue 3 Composition API syntax: create a function called App with a setup function that returns an object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined with a setup function, ready to use the composable in the next step.
successCriteria: App component is defined with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the App component with a setup function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you define a function named App with a setup function inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function named App with a setup function.

steps.title: Use the useWindowSize composable in the App component
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, call the useWindowSize composable function and destructure the width and height values from its return object.
steps.hint: Call useWindowSize() and use destructuring assignment to get width and height, similar to: const { width, height } = useWindowSize();
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: using a composable in a component
const { data, loading } = useFetchData();
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component's setup function now calls useWindowSize and obtains reactive width and height values.
successCriteria: useWindowSize is called inside setup, and width and height are destructured from its return object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully called the useWindowSize composable and obtained the reactive window dimensions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useWindowSize() inside the setup function and using destructuring to get width and height.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useWindowSize composable hasn't been called in the App component. Try calling it inside setup() and destructuring the returned values.

steps.title: Display the window dimensions in the template
steps.instruction: Return a template from the App component's setup function that displays the current width and height values using double curly braces {{ }} interpolation.
steps.hint: In Vue's setup function, you can return an object containing the reactive values you want to use in the template. Then in the template section, use {{ width }} and {{ height }} to display their current values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a template that displays the current window width and height values, which will update automatically when the window is resized.
successCriteria: The App component returns a template that uses {{ width }} and {{ height }} interpolation to display the reactive window dimensions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully displayed the reactive window dimensions in the template. The values will automatically update when the window is resized.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your template uses the correct interpolation syntax {{ }} to display both width and height values from the setup function's return object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template isn't displaying the window dimensions correctly. Remember to return width and height from the setup function and use {{ }} interpolation in the template to show their values.
